$comment: Registered exceptions to constitution VII's stage-layer rule, enforced by
and again at release-dispatch time from release.yml's Gate 1b.
A workflow_call-only stage is the PUBLISHED CONTRACT: it owns no trigger
and reads no ambient repository state. Every deviation lives here, in the
open, with a reason and a tracking issue -- never as a name missing from a
list, and never as a code comment alone. watchdog.yml's exception used to
be expressed by NOT APPEARING in release.yml's brace expansion, while its
own comment called itself 'release.yml Gate 1b's documented vars.*-read
exception' and release.yml never mentioned the watchdog (#149).
Every entry is STALE-CHECKED in both directions. A pattern that matches
nothing fails the gate, so a waiver cannot outlive its reason. A `count`
that no longer matches fails the gate, so a waived deviation can neither
grow nor quietly widen past the deviation it covers. Changing a count is
therefore a deliberate, reviewed act -- which is the point: at v2.2.0
every stage the old gate DID cover read vars.* exactly zero times, so a
waiver should feel uncomfortable to hold.

waivers.reason: The watchdog's fourteen repository-variable reads: five branch prefixes twice over (specs/018), one model override (WING_COMMANDER_DIAGNOSE_MODEL), the self-dispatch cap, and WING_COMMANDER_WATCHDOG_PAUSED -- the last of these a deliberately DEPRECATED shim (#152). The real pause kill switch now lives in the two wrapper workflows, where it stops a run before any agent bills; the stage-side read is retained only because it ships in v2.1.0, so removing it alone would be a breaking change spent on one read out of fourteen. Count lowered 15 -> 14 by specs/024-watchdog-precision-hardening: removing the propose-fix step took WING_COMMANDER_IMPLEMENT_MODEL, the second model override, with it. This is the gate working as designed -- a waiver must not stay wider than the deviation it covers -- and the first of the reads this waiver said would go. The rest go together in the watchdog rework's major (#149). Until then the count is the guard rail: #149 measured these reads growing 2 -> 9 -> 15 across four tagged releases with the release-time gate passing every time, because watchdog.yml was not in the eight-file list it grepped. A fifteenth read fails this gate on the pull request that introduces it.
